extracted.intended_audience: prospective and current NIMH K-series (mentored) career development applicants and awardees
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and policy requirements for preparing, submitting, transferring, and managing NIMH mentored career development (K-series) applications and awards (e.g., K99/R00, K01, K08, K23, K22, K24).

rubrics_metrics.name: Early consultation with NIMH Research Training and Career Development representative
rubrics_metrics.description: Prospective applicants are strongly encouraged to consult with the NIMH Research Training and Career Development representative in the appropriate Division well in advance of preparing an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Program Officer will discuss the relevance of the proposed research to the Institute's priorities, provide guidance on research and training plans, and help identify the most appropriate funding opportunity for the research and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct programmatic and grants-management questions to appropriate contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees should direct programmatic questions to the responsible Program Officer and grants management questions to the Grants Specialist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both individuals’ contact information is available in the Principal Investigator’s eRA Commons account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction in the Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction in RCR is an integral component of any career development program and successful completion is required during Year 01 of any NIMH career development award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructional details must be reported in the Year 02 Progress Report; see NIMH guidance for Responsible Conduct of Research Training Requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum effort (percent effort) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each K program requires recipients to devote a defined, minimum percentage of full-time professional effort to research and career development activities during the award period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants/awardees must consult the Table of K Parameters for the minimum effort requirements for each specific K program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate mentored K support limit (institutional + individual)
rubrics_metrics.description: If initially supported by an institutional mentored career development program, NIMH may allow— in aggregate— up to six years of mentored K support from a combination of institutional and individual mentored career development awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The total period is expected to provide sufficient time for transition to independence; applicants must justify the need for additional mentored K support in their individual mentored K application. All other individual mentored award rules still apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research effort policy during the last two years of individual mentored K support
rubrics_metrics.description: During the last two years of mentored K support (K01, K08, K23), NIH policy permits awardees to reduce career development effort to no less than 6 person-months (50%) and replace that effort with effort as a PI on a peer-reviewed research award or as a project leader on a competing multi-project award, provided the PI remains in a mentored situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy (NOT-OD-08-065 and NOT-OD-18-157) is intended to allow awardees ready to compete for research grants to continue benefiting from protected time. Note: this policy does not apply to K99 awardees. The total level of research commitment must remain at 9 person-months or more for the duration of the mentored K award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of institution — general transfer policy
rubrics_metrics.description: NIMH will consider transfers from one institution to another with prior approval of the responsible Program Officer, subject to specific conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: K99 transfers are allowed only when the K99 PI and mentor transfer to the same institution. Transfers are not allowed when less than six months remain in the project period at the time of the change-of-institution application, during an administrative extension, or after an award has terminated. Early consultation with NIMH staff is critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of institution — application instructions and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A change of institution application must be submitted in response to PA-24-254 by the authorized organizational representative at the new institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application should be submitted at least three months before the desired effective date to allow time for staff review. Applications requesting change of institution submitted after July 15th will generally not be reviewed until the next fiscal year (after October 1st).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for approving transfer of career awards without peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Transfers may be approved without peer review only after Program Officer assessment of key factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program Officer will assess: degree to which original goals will be met at the new institution; continued capacity to carry out full-time research; research productivity; likelihood the new environment will contribute to scientific development and productivity; scientific/technical merit of the research plan and consistency with the career development plan; new mentor's research and mentoring qualifications (if applicable); and institutional environment and commitment. The Program Officer then recommends approval or disapproval to the Grants Management Specialist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Human Subjects and Data & Safety Monitoring requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Application’s Protection of Human Subjects section and Data and Safety Monitoring Plan must reflect NIMH and NIH policies and federal regulations (see NOT-MH-19-027).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans for protection of subjects and data/safety monitoring will be reviewed by NIMH for consistency with NIMH/NIH policy and federal regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting recruitment milestones for clinical research
rubrics_metrics.description: NIMH requires reporting of recruitment milestones for extramural-funded clinical research studies proposing to enroll 150 or more participants, and for all clinical trials regardless of number of participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expectation will be stated in the Notice of Award (NoA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and results reporting for NIMH-supported clinical trials
rubrics_metrics.description: NIMH expects registration and results reporting for all NIMH-supported clinical trials, regardless of whether they are subject to FDAAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expectation will be stated in the Notice of Award.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH clinical trial definition and NOFO submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH defines a clinical trial as a study in which participants are prospectively assigned to interventions to evaluate effects on health-related outcomes (NOT-OD-15-015). Applications involving one or more independent clinical trials must be submitted through a NOFO specifically designated as 'Clinical Trial Required', 'Clinical Trial Optional', or 'Basic Experimental Studies with Humans'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources (case studies, FAQs, decision tool) are available to help determine whether a study is an NIH-defined clinical trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIMH experimental therapeutics approach for intervention research
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentored career development applications in intervention development/testing must be designed to assess the relationship between underlying disease processes and the mechanisms of action through which an intervention produces therapeutic change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must include examination of a hypothesized mechanism of action or proximal target based on evidence of disease processes, present a clear hypothesis linking intervention-driven changes in the target to improvement in clinical endpoints, and address safety and tolerability. Applicants are encouraged to review related NIMH funding opportunity announcements for fuller descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation to measure target engagement and use multiple units of analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies testing whether a novel intervention engages and alters the hypothesized mechanism/target should consider assessing target engagement and change using multiple units of analysis (e.g., genetic, neural circuits, physiology, behavior, self-report).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination of which units to use depends on the scientific hypothesis and feasibility. The specific activities and milestones depend on intervention type (behavioral, drug, device) and stage of development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phased approach encouraged for intervention development
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may use a phased approach where phase 1 supports testing/validating the intervention’s mechanism of action (target identification and engagement), followed by additional studies relating mechanism to functional/clinical effects (phase 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not using a phased approach, studies must still include a mechanism of action (treatment target) as part of the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority consequences for not proposing mechanism assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants that do not propose assessment of a mechanism of action and its engagement as part of the research protocol will be viewed as low program priority under NIMH intervention development requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to include mechanism assessment reduces program priority regardless of study design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot studies of novel interventions — expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot studies where there is already evidence of target engagement should evaluate feasibility and acceptability of the intervention in a patient population and evaluate the relationship between change in the targeted mechanism and change in functional or clinical status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to specific NIMH FOAs (e.g., R33 Clinical Trial Required) for complete descriptions of expectations for pilot intervention work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness research expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Research on effectiveness of therapeutic, preventive, and services interventions (including pilot studies) should be designed to explicitly address and re-confirm whether the intervention targets and mechanisms identified under efficacy conditions are operative in the effectiveness (broader/community) context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designs should test whether mechanisms translate to broader target populations or settings prior to larger-scale studies; see related NIMH FOAs (e.g., R34) for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Data Management and Sharing (DMS) policy applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications submitted after January 25, 2023, the NIH DMS policy applies to some career development awards (e.g., K01, K08, K23, K99, K22).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators and institutions are expected to plan and budget for data management and sharing, submit a DMS plan for review when applying, and comply with the approved DMS plan (see 2023 Final NIH Policy for DMS and NIMH NOT-MH-23-100). Note: K awardees are not required to deposit data into the NIMH Data Archive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select the appropriate K funding mechanism/NOFO
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must apply to the appropriate K funding opportunity for their stage and project (e.g., K99, K22, K01, K08, K23, K24, tenure-track K22), and Program Officer can help identify the most appropriate funding opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links to specific funding opportunity information and examples of funded awards (NIH RePORTER) are available; applicants should align project scope and career-development plan with the chosen K mechanism's constraints and parameters.
